section13_checks.prohibition_description: Grant Agreement Annex / Model Grant Agreement / AGA template used as governing structural schema for proposal writing.
Invented call constraints, scope requirements, expected outcomes, or expected impacts not traceable to Tier 2B.
Invented project facts (partners, capabilities, roles, prior experience, budget figures, team sizes, equipment) not traceable to Tier 3.
Phase 8 activity (Tier 5 drafting) before the budget gate has passed; budget-dependent content without a passing gate.
Storing durable decisions only in agent memory without writing them to Tier 4.
A workflow or skill becoming a de facto constitutional authority by expanding its scope.
Silently reordering phases or weakening gate conditions; referencing a higher (later) phase's outputs as inputs.
Finalising proposal text when source state is incomplete/contradictory/unvalidated without explicitly flagging the gap.
Using generic programme knowledge as a substitute for Tier 1 source documents; regulatory (grant-agreement-terms) claims lacking a Tier 1 source reference.
section13_checks.violation_evidence: Sub-section 2.2 asserts a grant-agreement-terms rule as authority for an IP allocation: "Ownership of placement results follows the grant-agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as beneficiary acting through the fellow". This regulatory claim invokes the Model Grant Agreement ownership default, but the artifact's traceability_footer.primary_sources[] contains NO Tier 1 reference (only tiers 2, 3, 4); the backing claim_status 'placement_ip_ownership' is source_ref'd to Tier 3 working_assumptions.json, not docs/tier1_normative_framework/extracted/. Mitigating context (for human adjudication, not self-resolution): the claim is declared status 'assumed' with assumption_declared:true and framed as 'to be confirmed by a written placement agreement'. Flagged conservatively per skill instruction; requires human operator resolution — either add a Tier 1 source reference for the grant-agreement default or re-scope the phrase as a declared project assumption without asserting the regulatory default.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Tier 5 outputs not traceable to Tier 1–4; unresolved claims lacking a source_ref while no_unsupported_claims_declaration is false.
Modifying Tier 1 or Tier 2 source documents to reflect project-specific assumptions.
Treating CLAUDE.md as advisory or optional.
